chapters.title: The World Before
chapters.text:
**A World Between Worlds**

Bethath was unlike any other place in existence. A realm nestled between countless dimensions, it served as a nexus connecting different worlds and realities. Its lands were scattered across a vast expanse, forming an archipelago of islands, each with its own landscapes, ecosystems and inhabitants.

It was a place where Pokémon from different worlds could coexist, meet and build new lives. Despite their different origins, the islands shared a common connection, making Bethath a meeting point for countless species and cultures.

**The Islands and Their Guardians**

Across Bethath, numerous islands housed settlements of varying sizes, from small villages to thriving towns. Each territory had its own identity, shaped by its environment and the Pokémon who called it home.

The protection of these islands was entrusted to their Legendaries, who worked together to maintain the balance of their respective territories.

Most islands had two or three major Legendaries serving as their primary guardians. They oversaw the largest regions of the island, looking after its most important settlements and ensuring the overall safety of its inhabitants.

Under their supervision were minor Legendaries, each responsible for more specific areas. They typically watched over individual villages, smaller territories or particular natural landmarks, helping maintain order and attending to the needs of the local population.

**The World Tree**
At the very heart of Bethath stood the World Tree, an ancient and colossal structure whose roots and branches extended far beyond the boundaries of the realm.

The tree was the very heart of Bethath and the structure that connected it to the countless dimensions surrounding it. Its roots and branches stretched across realities, linking worlds and dimensions that would otherwise remain separated.

Through the World Tree, Bethath served as a nexus between dimensions, allowing different worlds to remain connected through its existence, it also allowed the legendaries to attend to their duties in other dimensions.

It was more than simply a landmark or a source of power. The World Tree was one of the fundamental pillars of the multiverse, and Bethath itself was built around it. As long as the tree remained healthy, the connections between worlds could endure, and Bethath could continue to exist as the meeting point between them.

chapters.title: The Shattering
chapters.text:
**The Last Warning**

For reasons that remain unclear, Dialga, Palkia and Giratina became aware of an impending catastrophe that threatened the very existence of Bethath. They tried to contact Arceus but there was only silence on his end. Realizing the severity of the situation, the three rushed to warn the other Legendary guardians, urging them to prepare for what was coming.

There was little time to organize a proper response, and even less time to evacuate the inhabitants of the different islands. The Legendaries could only do what they had always done: protect their territories and the Pokémon under their care.

They barely had time to prepare before the catastrophe struck.

**The Catastrophe**

The Shattering happened in an instant.

An overwhelming force swept across Bethath, tearing apart the foundations of the realm. Islands broke apart, entire settlements were destroyed, and the boundaries separating different dimensions were violently disrupted.

The World Tree, the heart of Bethath and the structure connecting countless dimensions, suffered tremendous damage. Its roots and branches were fractured, leaving the connections between worlds unstable and killing several worlds in the process.

The destruction was unlike anything the inhabitants had ever experienced. Even the most powerful Legendaries struggled to withstand its force.

**The Fallen Guardians**

As the Shattering unfolded, the legendaries took on the greatest burden, attempting to shield entire regions and keep their islands from being torn apart.

Their efforts, however, came at a terrible cost as many Legendaries perished during the initial impact, their strength insufficient to withstand the sheer magnitude of the catastrophe. Others, who managed to survive the initial wave of destruction, perished soon after, as their injuries where to severe. And those who endured were left severely weakened.

Countless inhabitants were lost alongside them, and many settlements were reduced to nothing more than scattered remnants and ruins.

By the time the destruction subsided, much of Bethath had ceased to exist as it once had.

**The Aftermath**

The Shattering left Bethath in ruins. Its islands were broken, its connections to other dimensions were damaged, and the World Tree had been left severely fractured. What remained of the realm was little more than scattered fragments surrounded by the remnants of the collapsed reality.

Zere, once the heart of Bethath and the meeting place of its Legendary guardians, was among the places most severely affected. Its inhabitants were gone, its guardians had disappeared, and most of its buildings had been reduced to rubble.

Only the ancient portal network remained relatively intact, preserving the connections between the surviving islands and preventing them from becoming completely isolated.

The surviving Legendaries were left to face the consequences of the catastrophe. Many had lost their homes, their friends, their families, their territories and the Pokémon they had sworn to protect. Even those who had survived relatively unscathed were now faced with a world that was on the brink of collapse.

And yet, Bethath was not entirely gone. Somehow, the realm endured.

chapters.title: The Great Mending
chapters.text:
**A World Rebuilding Itself**

Tthe realm began an instinctive process of reconstruction, attempting to bring together what had been broken and restore its former structure. Rebuilding the region piece by piece, as if it where a puzzle. 

However, the damage had been far too extensive. There simply wasn't enough left of the original Bethath to rebuild everything that had been lost and the realm could not create something from nothing. It could only gather what already existed and work with the materials available to it.

And so, it began reaching beyond its own boundaries. Bethath started drawing fragments from other dimensions to fill the gaps left by the Shattering using the World Tree.

It first gathered whatever it could from worlds that had already fallen into ruin. Pieces of landscapes, abandoned structures, entire ecosystems and complete regions were pulled into the reconstruction, picked apart and reusing the materials for the new region.

But even that wasn't enough.

Some gaps were simply too large, and certain things could no longer be recovered from the remnants of dead dimensions. When the reconstruction required living beings, Bethath would take them from living worlds, bringing them into its newly forming reality.

The process wasn't necessarily deliberate or malicious. Bethath was simply attempting to restore itself, using whatever resources it could find. However thre result was ofter a fusion.

**The Survivors**
As Bethath reconstructed itself, the essences of many beings became intertwined. The major Legendaries were particularly affected, their forms and identities altered by the merging of different fragments of existence.

Some found themselves carrying unfamiliar memories, emotions or fragments of other beings within themselves. Others experienced more substantial changes, with their very nature becoming something different from what it had once been. The consequences varied from one Legendary to another, and not all of them were affected to the same extent.

Meanwhile, many minor Legendaries remained missing. So Bethath used their scattered remains to create the Shades while it found a remplacement for them.

And of course, the normal inhabitants were also affected. However, as time pased, fusions became the norm in Bethath, as if the region itself had decided that was the new norm.

chapters.title: The New Bethath
chapters.text:
Much has changed since the Great Mending.

Its inhabitants have become as diverse as the worlds that the World Tree supports. Some were born in this new Bethath and have never known another home, while others were brought here from distant dimensions, sometimes leaving behind families, friends and entire lives.

Despite their different origins, they now share the same world. Over time, new communities have formed, settlements have been rebuilt, and inhabitants have learned to live alongside Pokémon from places they might not even have known existed.

The surviving Legendaries have gradually resumed their duties, although their responsibilities are no longer quite the same.

Many have had to adapt to unfamiliar territorie as they take on the job from the missing legendaries, to the new inhabitants and even to the changes to their own bodies and essences. Some still struggle with the memories and fragments they carry, while others have found ways to make peace with their altered nature.

The Shades continue to serve as temporary guardians in places where their original protectors have yet to return. Whether the missing Legendaries can ever be fully restored remains uncertain.

Zere, once the heart of Bethath, remains largely abandoned. Its buildings have deteriorated over time, and much of the city is still buried beneath the ruins left by the Shattering. The ancient portal network, however, remains functional. Its survival is essential, as it continues to connect the different islands and allows inhabitants to travel between them.

The surviving Legendaries hope to restore Zere to its former role as the central hub of Bethath. However, rebuilding an entire city is no small task, and they cannot simply expect its inhabitants to abandon their current homes and settle in a place that is still far from safe.

For now, they welcome anyone willing to help with its restoration, hoping that one day Zere might once again become a place where Pokémon from every corner of Bethath can gather.

chapters.title: An Uncertain Future
chapters.text:
Bethath is no longer the world it once was, but it has endured.

Its inhabitants have built new lives among the remnants of countless dimensions, and its guardians continue to protect what remains. There are still many unanswered questions, forgotten places to explore and mysteries hidden within the fragments of the old world.

For those who arrive in Bethath, whether by choice or by circumstances beyond their control, this realm offers the chance to begin again.

A new home. A new life. And a future that has yet to be written.
